points.description: States that the height of a tree is a length/count of a path (e.g., number of edges on the path), not the total number of nodes in the tree or the depth of one particular node. Accept wording such as 'longest path' only if it clearly refers to the path's length.
Identifies that the path used is the longest one, i.e. the maximum-length path among the paths in the tree.
States that the path starts at the root of the tree.
States that the path ends at a leaf (any leaf) of the tree.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all four elements: height is a path length, the path is the longest, it starts at the root, and it ends at a leaf. Award each point only when that element is explicitly present or clearly implied; missing one element loses that point. No marks for defining height as the shortest path, the total number of nodes, or the depth of a single node.
